result.output:
Held as a draft: **blocked on UAT, which is blocked on #1253.**

CI is green and CodeRabbit's verdict on `71e1d1405` is clean. What is outstanding is not a code review — it is the one claim in this PR that only a human at a browser can settle, and settling it needs a working login.

## What is unverified

Whether an ordinary browser saves the **file's own bytes** or the app shell. `useFileDownload` mints a `/stream/<ticket>` URL and clicks an anchor; if the Service Worker does not intercept that request, the origin answers it with the SPA fallback and the member receives a 394-byte `index.html` under the file's name, with no error surfaced. Filed as #1247.

It cannot be settled inside Playwright, because Playwright's own CDP download capture is the suspect. It needs a real browser, a real session, DevTools open, and a check that the worker is **controlling** the page before the click — if it is not, `MediaService.streaming` is false, `streamTicket` returns null, and `save` quietly takes the buffered blob path, which works correctly and proves nothing about the path under suspicion.

## Why it is blocked

Login is down on every method. Google returns `401 invalid_client` because the Web3Auth project client ID is passed where the provider's belongs; wallet dead-ends at `NotStarted`; passwordless email is Web3Auth's rather than ours. All three are #1253, and the Google half specifically is #1256 — the one piece that is independent of the ADR and can land on its own.

## What this PR does not depend on

Nothing here rests on that verification. The round trip asserts through the preview path (buffered `facade.download`) rather than the save affordance, precisely because the save path is under suspicion — so the byte assertion never touches it. #1247 records that the workaround should be removed once the save path is trusted.

Flip back to ready once a session can be created and the check is run.

name: web-e2e-local-full-suite-recipe
description: "How to get a trustworthy local full web-e2e run — env alignment, fresh dev servers, and the two known external failure signatures"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 064836b9-90e4-42d5-aabc-ed5fde831a57
---

Running the full 208-spec `tests/web-e2e` suite locally (learned 2026-07-03, phase 68.1 exit gates):

- **API env**: the API dev process MUST export `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production` (the sdk-e2e harness default) — a mismatched/other value 401s `recovery.spec.ts` and any test-login caller, masking their real state. Start: `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001 pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`.
- **Fresh dev servers**: restart vite (and rebuild `sdk-core`/`sdk` dists first) before a gate run — a multi-day vite process caused roving `wallet-login-button` timeouts; vite also serves stale sdk code after dist rebuilds unless restarted.
- **Web3Auth Core Kit external flake** (~2-3 files per full run, roving): signatures are the login-page toast `Failed to get vault keypair from Core Kit` and a raw Torus quorum banner `Unable to resolve enough promises`. NOT our code — `wallet-login-helpers.ts` has bounded retry (68.1-25/29), but it can still exceed the budget. Disposition: single-file re-run once; green = external flake.
- **Serial cascade**: every spec file is `describe.serial` — one failure skips the rest of its file ("N did not run" ≠ global abort). Judge coverage by first-failures per file + single-file re-runs, not the raw did-not-run count.
- **Capture discipline**: redirect the run to a log and append `EXIT_CODE=$?`; never pipe through `tail`/`tee` (masks exit codes). Playwright wipes `test-results/` per run — harvest failure screenshots BEFORE any re-run. This config writes no usable `.last-run.json` for full runs — don't build watchdogs on it.
- Full run ≈ 17-20 min (M-series, workers=1). Related: [[bg-executor-lost-wake-continuation]] — executors that background the suite run may lose their wake; nudge via SendMessage with the tally.

name: project-local-login-config-from-gh-actions-vars
description: "The Web3Auth and Google login config for local UAT lives in GitHub Actions variables, not in any committed file"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: ff3a17b8-94b6-4c1b-94ab-5253b0600f57
  modified: 2026-08-16T13:38:21.323Z
---

No committed file holds the Web3Auth or Google identifiers a local interactive
login needs. Read them from the repo's GitHub Actions variables instead of
asking the user:

- `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/actions/variables` gives
  `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `REDACTED`.
- `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/environments/staging/variables`
  gives a `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` that already lists `tauri://localhost`.

The project's real Google client is
`164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee`, which holds `localhost:5173`,
`app-staging.cipherbox.cc`, `cipher-box.onrender.com`, `localhost:1420` and the
three `http://127.0.0.1:1420{0,1,2}/callback` entries.

Until 2026-08-16 the staging `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` variable named
`959751863260-j1u1…` instead — a client that rejects both
`https://app-staging.cipherbox.cc` and the desktop loopback URI, so staging
Google sign-in failed with `redirect_uri_mismatch`. The variable is now
corrected, but a redeploy is what makes it take effect.

`desktop-staging-release.yml` feeds `vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` into
`VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, so web and desktop use one Google client.
`VITE_ENVIRONMENT=local` maps to `WEB3AUTH_NETWORK.DEVNET`, the network those
variables belong to.

**Why:** the values are variables rather than secrets, so they are readable, and
guessing or asking wastes a round trip.

**How to apply:** for a desktop or web local login run, pull the four values
this way. `apps/api/.env` must also carry `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and list
`tauri://localhost` in `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, or the identity exchange from a
packaged Tauri webview is refused. See
[[project-desktop-uat-stack-recipe]].

name: feedback-leave-docker-stack-running
description: "Don't tear down the shared cipherbox docker stack after ship/e2e — leave it running"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 60afe4f5-90e8-4017-b046-ab86ca19c540
---

After a ship/e2e run, do NOT bring down the `cipherbox-infrastructure` docker
compose stack (`docker/docker-compose.yml`: ipfs/kubo, someguy, postgres, redis,
mock-ipns-routing) or standalone dev containers like `byo-ipfs-kubo`. Only clean
up session-specific processes you started — e.g. the ship-started API-from-dist
on :3000.

**Why:** the docker stack is shared infrastructure that other sessions/processes
may be using; tearing it down disrupts them and forces a slow rebuild/restart.

**How to apply:** on cleanup, `kill` the :3000 API (and any other process this
session spawned) but leave `docker compose down` out of it unless the user
explicitly asks to stop docker. Relates to [[project-web-e2e-local-full-suite-recipe]].

name: project-api-restart-masked-by-eaddrinuse
description: A failed local API restart is masked because the old process keeps serving port 3000 and answers the health check
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ff3a17b8-94b6-4c1b-94ab-5253b0600f57
  modified: 2026-08-14T12:47:48.798Z
---

`pkill -f 'nest start'` does not stop the local API. The process command is
`node -r ts-node/register src/main.ts`, so the pattern matches nothing. The new
process then dies with `EADDRINUSE` on port 3000 while the **old** one keeps
answering `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`, so the restart looks successful and
the new configuration never takes effect.

This cost a debugging cycle on 2026-08-14: a stale API kept an old
`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` from an inline environment override, and every Google login
died at `google-oauth.service.ts:51` with the generic
`Google token verification failed`, which names no audience.

**Why:** a health check proves that *something* serves the port, never that it
is the process just started.

**How to apply:** stop with `pkill -f 'ts-node/register src/main.ts'`. After any
restart, assert the listener changed — `lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN -t` —
and grep the log for `EADDRINUSE`. Prefer editing `apps/api/.env` over an inline
override, because an override outlives the file and is invisible in it.

# Web E2E

The PR gate's smoke slice: `apps/web` driven in a real browser against a real
API, a real engine, and the hermetic `/routing/v1` record store. Wired as the
merge-blocking `Web E2E Smoke` job (`.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml`), reported
through the stable `Web E2E Smoke Result` context in `ci.yml`.

Normative source: [`blueprint/testing.md`](../../blueprint/testing.md).

## What it covers

- the front door renders every built login method
- an unauthenticated deep link is returned to the front door and lists no vault
  contents
- a cold start reaches a settled, empty vault at its root; the chrome renders
  it, and the event taps saw the snapshot that produced it
- signing out returns the tab to the front door
- the shipping bundle exposes no introspection hook

## What it does not cover yet

Nothing on the write path — no folder create/rename/move/delete, no upload, no
download. `blueprint/testing.md` scopes this tier at login-and-CRUD, and the
CRUD half is blocked on engine and workflow work outside this suite. The issue
tracker carries what is outstanding and why.

## How the suite logs in

There is no interactive Core Kit login in CI. The `e2e` build carries the
introspection hook (`apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts`), which hands the
engine a login secret the test generates. Challenge-signature login creates the
account on first contact, so each test's fresh 32-byte secret is a fresh,
isolated vault — no fixture setup and no shared state to serialize around.

The `release` project runs the same specs' counterpart against a bundle built
**without** the flag, and asserts `window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__` is absent.

## Running it locally

Both bundles must be built before Playwright starts; the config only serves
them.

1. Bring up Postgres and the record store:

   ```sh
   docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres mock-ipns-routing
   ```

2. Apply migrations and boot the API:

   ```sh
   export DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME=postgres \
     DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED DB_DATABASE=cipherbox NODE_ENV=test \
     JWT_SECRET=web-e2e-jwt-secret THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200 \
     CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:4173,http://localhost:4174
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build && node apps/api/dist/main.js
   ```

3. Build both bundles:

   ```sh
   export VITE_ENVIRONMENT=ci VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
     VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS=http://localhost:3001
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:wasm
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   mv apps/web/dist apps/web/dist-release
   VITE_E2E_HOOK=true pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
   ```

4. Run the suite:

   ```sh
   pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e
   ```

   The script is `test:e2e`, not `test`: the workspace-wide `Test` gate runs no
   suite that needs a live stack.

Rebuild the bundle after any `apps/web` change — the suite serves `dist/`, not
a dev server.

---
#!/bin/sh
# CipherBox Kubo init: announce only pin roots to the DHT, not every block.
#
# Reduces background provide/reprovide CPU on the shared Kubo node. With the
# default "all" strategy the staging node scheduled ~76k CIDs for DHT
# announcement, consuming a large share of Kubo's CPU at idle; "roots" cuts that
# to the pin-root count (~18k) with no loss of retrievability (every pinned root
# is still announced; only unpinned intermediate blocks are dropped).
#
# Kubo 0.40 renamed Reprovider.Strategy -> Provide.Strategy. This file is sourced
# by the Kubo entrypoint on every boot (before the daemon starts), so the setting
# is idempotent and survives container recreation and fresh repos.
ipfs config Provide.Strategy roots || echo "ipfs-init: failed to set Provide.Strategy roots (continuing)"

    image: postgres:16-alpine

      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-postgres}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE:-cipherbox}
    ports:
      - '${DB_PORT:-5432}:5432'
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U postgres']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  ipfs:
    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
    container_name: cipherbox-ipfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - IPFS_PATH=/data/ipfs
      # pebbleds: LSM-tree datastore for faster concurrent write throughput (Phase 19.2)
      # Requires fresh IPFS repo -- delete ipfs_data volume before first start:
      #   docker compose down -v --remove-orphans && docker compose up -d
      - IPFS_PROFILE=server,pebbleds
    volumes:
      - ipfs_data:/data/ipfs
      # Kubo runs /container-init.d/*.sh on every boot (sourced before the daemon);
      # 001-provide-strategy.sh sets Provide.Strategy=roots idempotently.
      - ./ipfs-init:/container-init.d:ro
    ports:

      - '4001:4001/udp'

# The web e2e smoke slice (blueprint/testing.md). The suite runs against the
# production static build, so it needs the engine WASM: a caller passes
# `wasm-artifact` to hand over the module its run already built, and a caller
# that does not gets the module built here. It builds the bundle twice: once as
# it ships, once with `VITE_E2E_HOOK` for the introspection seam. The suite
# asserts the shipping one carries no hook.
name: Web E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Git ref to checkout (tag, branch, or SHA)'
        required: false
        type: string
      wasm-artifact:
        description: >-
          Name of a run artifact holding a prebuilt engine WASM module. Set it
          and the suite tests exactly those bytes; leave it empty and this job
          builds the module itself, which is what a standalone dispatch needs.
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string

permissions: {}

jobs:
  web-e2e:
    name: Web E2E Smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The suite itself runs in seconds; the budget covers a standalone
    # dispatch, where a cold-cache wasm build runs ahead of it.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      # The write path's block store. Without it `KuboPinStore` refuses every
      # hosted upload with a 503, which the drain charges as a spent attempt —
      # so a write spec dead-letters rather than merely failing to publish.
      ipfs:
        image: ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0
        ports:
          - 5001:5001
          - 8080:8080
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "ipfs id"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
          --health-start-period 30s

    env:
      DB_HOST: localhost
      DB_PORT: 5432
      DB_USERNAME: postgres
      DB_PASSWORD: postgres
      DB_DATABASE: cipherbox_test
      JWT_SECRET: web-e2e-jwt-secret
      KUBO_API_URL: http://localhost:5001
      # Every test cold-starts its own account from one runner IP, so the
      # per-IP auth bucket would otherwise cap how many specs can exist.
      THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT: '200'
      CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://localhost:4173,http://localhost:4174
      # `ci` names no deployment, so the bundle needs no Web3Auth identifiers:
      # the suite hands the engine a login secret through the introspection seam
      # rather than through an interactive Core Kit session.
      VITE_ENVIRONMENT: ci
      VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
      # The hermetic record store, in place of the public default — a merge gate
      # must not resolve vault pointers over the internet.
      VITE_ROUTING_ENDPOINTS: http://localhost:3001
      # The same stack's gateway, so a read pulls its blocks back from where the
      # upload pinned them rather than from the tab that wrote them. By address,
      # not by name: Kubo serves `localhost` as a *subdomain* gateway and 301s
      # every path request to `<cid>.ipfs.localhost`, which resolves nowhere.
      VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}

      # Fail fast on a missing or malformed handover, before the stack boots.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact != ''
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.wasm-artifact }}
          path: apps/web/src/wasm

      # Same path set as `ci.yml`'s `Web Engine WASM` cache, for the same reason.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target/release
            target/wasm32-unknown-unknown
          key: web-e2e-cargo-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            web-e2e-cargo-
            main-wasm-cargo-

      - uses: ./.github/actions/wasm-bindgen-cli
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - uses: ./.github/actions/mock-ipns-routing

      # `NODE_ENV` stays on the API's own steps. Vite reads it to decide whether a
      # build is a production one, so job-wide it would hand the suite a
      # development bundle of the app it is meant to test as it ships.
      - name: Apply migrations to a fresh database
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api migration:run
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test

      - name: Build and boot the API
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
          node apps/api/dist/main.js > /tmp/api.log 2>&1 &
          curl -fsS --retry 60 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 http://localhost:3000/health \
            || { echo '--- API log ---'; cat /tmp/api.log; exit 1; }
        env:
          NODE_ENV: test

      # One engine module feeds both bundles below; only the hook flag differs
      # between them.
      - name: Build the engine WASM
        if: inputs.wasm-artifact == ''
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:wasm

      - name: Build the shipping bundle
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
          mv apps/web/dist apps/web/dist-release

      - name: Build the e2e bundle
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web run build:bundle
        env:
          VITE_E2E_HOOK: 'true'

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e exec playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Named `test:e2e`, not `test`: the workspace-wide `Test` gate runs no
      # suite that needs a live stack.
      - name: Run the web e2e smoke slice
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e

      - name: Upload the Playwright report on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: web-e2e-report
          path: |
            tests/web-e2e/playwright-report/
            tests/web-e2e/test-results/
          retention-days: 7

content.text:
The stack is up and the PR's new specs pass locally. Here is the state and the UAT script.

## What runs now

| Service | Address | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web, e2e bundle (has the console hook) | http://localhost:4173 | use this one for the UAT |
| Web, shipping bundle (no hook) | http://localhost:4174 | interactive login only |
| API | http://localhost:3000 | `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api dev`, pid 35852 |
| Mock `/routing/v1` store | http://localhost:3001 | host process, see the fix below |
| Kubo API / gateway | http://127.0.0.1:5001, http://127.0.0.1:8080 | docker, already up |
| Postgres | localhost:5432 | docker, migrations current |

I checked out `ci/web-e2e-write-path-and-cargo-cache-seed` at `71e1d1405` in the main tree. Your previous branch was `claude/cipher-box-1261-desktop-frontend`, and it is clean.

I ran the PR's new suite against this stack: **5 of 5 write-path specs pass** in 4.6 s.

## One repo defect blocked the stack

The `cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing` container was a stale image that sends no CORS headers, so every IPNS resolve from the browser failed with `net::ERR_FAILED` and all 5 specs timed out. A rebuild fails too: `docker/../tools/mock-ipns-routing/Dockerfile:12` runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which exits 1 on `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: esbuild@0.28.2`. I stopped the container and run `node tools/mock-ipns-routing/dist/index.js` on the host instead, which is what CI does. Tell me if you want an issue for the broken Dockerfile.

I also added `http://localhost:4173` and `http://localhost:4174` to `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in `apps/api/.env`.

## The manual UAT — issue #1247

The PR comment names one claim that only a human at a browser can settle: does an ordinary browser save the **file's own bytes**, or the app shell? The trap is that the buffered path also works, so a run that silently takes it proves nothing.

Open http://localhost:4173 in Chrome with DevTools open.

**Step 1 — create a session.** Google login needs a real account. The console hook is faster:

```js
const s = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
const hex = Array.from(s, b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
await window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__.signIn(hex);
```

A fresh secret makes a fresh vault. I ran this snippet here and it reaches `/files`.

**Step 2 — prove the worker controls the page.** Run this before any click:

```js
navigator.serviceWorker.controller !== null   // must be true
(await navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations()).map(r => [r.scope, r.active?.scriptURL, r.active?.state])
// expect ["http://localhost:4173/", ".../sw.js", "activated"]
```

If the controller is `null`, reload once and check again. A false value means `MediaService.streaming` is false, `streamTicket` returns null, and `save` takes the buffered blob path (`apps/web/src/lib/streamTicket.ts:14`). That path works and settles nothing.

**Step 3 — upload a file.** Use a file of a few KB with bytes you can recognize. Copy the row's `data-node-id` — that is the node hex.

**Step 4 — click Download with the Network tab filtered on `stream`.** Read the outcome:

- **Stream path, correct:** a request to `/stream/<uuid>`, status 200 or 206, with `cache-control: no-store`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `accept-ranges: bytes`.
- **The bug (#1247):** a `/stream/<uuid>` response of `content-type: text/html`, 394 bytes, without those headers. The origin answered with the SPA fallback. I confirmed with curl that the preview server returns exactly that for `/stream/<anything>`, so the worker is the only thing that stops it.
- **Buffered path, inconclusive:** no network request at all, and the anchor href starts with `blob:`. Go back to step 2.

Also watch for `[data-testid="vault-action-error"]` in the page.

**Step 5 — compare the bytes.** The engine's own read is the reference:

```js
await window.__CIPHERBOX_ENGINE__.download('<nodeHex>')   // plaintext as hex
```

Then check the saved file, for example `xxd -p ~/Downloads/<name> | tr -d '\n'`. A 394-byte HTML file is the failure. Equal bytes settle the claim.

The PR body records a second finding you can exercise the same way: a second forced refresh while a pass is in flight displaces it, and the queue then drains on neither.

- The `cipherbox-mock-ipns-routing` container image was stale and sends no CORS headers, so every browser resolve failed. Its Dockerfile also fails to rebuild (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exits 1 on `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: esbuild@0.28.2`). I run the store from source on the host instead, as CI does.

<result>## Root cause found — it is not provisioning. It is the read accelerator's new session bearer + browser CORS.

I reproduced it live in Chrome against the still-running local stack (web preview :4173, mock routing :3001, Kubo :8080) and traced it to the byte.

### The mechanism (proven, not inferred)

`892ca9981` (in your range) changed the accelerator's credential from *host-configured* to *the live session JWT*:

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1664` — `gateway: gateway.into_gateway(accelerator_bearer.clone())`, and `:1735` `.with_session_bearer(...)`, so `api.login_identity` at `:1739` fills the same cell.
- `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:219-230` — `into_gateway` attaches that bearer to the accelerator leg **if `carries_credentials_safely`**, and `:176-188` returns `true` for `localhost | 127.0.0.1 | [::1]` — the comment even says "a loopback host for local development (`apps/web/.env.example` ships a `http://localhost` Kubo)".
- `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:382-387` — every block fetch then carries `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.

At the base commit that bearer was `Option<Zeroizing<String>>` supplied by the host (`git show 4128ccc:crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:68`), and `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts:103-104` never supplied one — so the request went out unauthenticated.

An `Authorization` header makes the cross-origin GET non-simple. Kubo's gateway advertises `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Range, User-Agent, X-Requested-With` — **no `Authorization`**. Measured in the page itself:

```
Accept: application/vnd.ipld.raw               -> 200, 1052 bytes
Accept + Authorization: Bearer x               -> FAIL "Failed to fetch"   (preflight rejected)
```

`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` is unset in `apps/web/.env`, so the accelerator is the only source (`read.rs:166`, `:315-319` rotates on transport failure — there is nothing to rotate to). Every block read in the browser now fails.

### Answers

1. **No new provisioning gate is failing.** The real gates are: the resolve-tick loop spawns only with a root name (`facade.rs:2192`), and the drain leg runs only when *both* scope seeds are cached (`facade.rs:2388-2390`). Both were satisfied in my repro. What blocks the publish is one step later: `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) needs the root's head block through the gateway (`assemble_head_envelope`) and returns `Halt::UploadAttempt` when it cannot — silently, no dead letter. The same gateway failure makes `RootAdopter` fail, which the tick maps to `RefreshVerdict::Unreachable` → the exact string you saw (`facade.rs:2640`).

2. **All-zero root id is legitimate.** `facade.rs:1669` seeds `Snapshot::new(NodeId([0u8; 16]))`, and `facade.rs:2227`: "The vault's own root scope and root node are the anchored all-zero id16". It is not an unprovisioned tell.

3. **`handOffLoginSecret` is identical on both paths and the hook is missing no facade call.** Both `packages/login/src/flow.ts` (`handOff`) and `apps/web/src/engine/introspection.ts` call `handOffLoginSecret(facade, exporter)` → `facade.start(secret)` (`packages/login/src/secret.ts:63-73`). Provisioning lives *inside* `start` (`facade.rs:1779`). Live proof: the hook login minted the vault — no `vaultUnprovisioned` event was emitted (the event does cross the bridge: `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:748`), and the mock routing log shows the mint's two PUTs (root record then vault pointer, both 200) followed by the tick loop GETting the root name 200/310 bytes every cadence. The app's own path only adds the API identity exchange before Core Kit; the engine does its own `api.login_identity` either way.

4. **No test can see this.** `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs:578` builds engines on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` (which skips provisioning by design, `facade.rs:1776-1779`) and plants records, so "first-run mint → queued write drains" is never composed. The gateway tests use a scripted HTTP fake and assert only that the header is *present* (`read.rs:506` "accelerator request carries the member bearer token"). CORS is browser-only, and the wasm suite's new test just proves a host-supplied bearer is refused (`crates/wasm/src/host.rs`). Your web-e2e write-path specs are the first thing in the repo that could catch it.

5. **Root cause, one sentence:** since `892ca9981` the engine stamps the session JWT onto every read-accelerator request — including a loopback Kubo, which `carries_credentials_safely` explicitly permits — and the browser's CORS preflight for `Authorization` is rejected by that gateway, so no block can be read, the root never adopts, and the drain halts in `load_scope_root` before it publishes.

**Smallest fix — it is main's regression, and the one-liner belongs in `crates/engine`:** in `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:176-188`, stop treating a loopback accelerator as credential-safe (fall to `GatewaySource::public(base_url)`, `read.rs:227`). No browser will ever deliver an `Authorization` header to a plain local gateway, so the loopback exemption can only ever break reads — and it also stops shipping the session token to a gateway that isn't CipherBox's. Staging/prod are `https://` and unaffected.

Caller-side alternatives if you want the loopback exemption kept: move the Kubo URL from `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` to `VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` in `apps/web/.env`(+`.env.example`, + the web-e2e CI env), or add `Authorization` to Kubo's `Gateway.HTTPHeaders` CORS allowlist in the compose file. Either unblocks the specs, but neither protects the next host that points the accelerator at a gateway it doesn't control.

One thing to check separately: whatever real accelerator staging uses must allowlist `Authorization` in its CORS response, or the web app will fail there the same way.</result>

content.text:
The diagnosis is proven end-to-end. With `Authorization` allowed on the local Kubo gateway, the rebased head passes **11 of 11** e2e specs in 5.5 s — the same head that failed 5 of 5 minutes earlier.

**Root cause.** `892ca9981` (#1243, in the rebase range) sources the read-accelerator bearer from the session. `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:174-189` treats a loopback accelerator as credential-safe, so the engine stamps `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every block read to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. That makes the request non-simple, and Kubo's gateway advertises no `Authorization` in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, so the browser preflight rejects it. No block reads, the root never adopts, and `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) halts before it publishes — with no dead letter, which is why the UI reads `synced` while the write sits pending forever.

This hits CI as well: `web-e2e.yml:90` sets `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080` against a stock Kubo service. So the rebased branch fails its own gate until something changes. Two other consequences: the loopback rule sends a session token to any gateway the host does not own, and staging's real accelerator must allow `Authorization` in CORS or the web app fails there the same way.

The rebase is committed locally and unpushed. Where the fix lands decides whether I push now.

input.content:
Since #1243 the engine stamps the member's session JWT onto every read-accelerator request, and `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs` treats a loopback accelerator as able to keep it:

```rust
matches!(host, "localhost" | "127.0.0.1" | "[::1]")
```

No browser can deliver that header to such a gateway. `Authorization` makes the cross-origin block read non-simple, and a stock Kubo gateway answers the preflight with

```
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Range, User-Agent, X-Requested-With
```

which omits it. Measured in the page against the local stack:

| request | result |
| --- | --- |
| `Accept: application/vnd.ipld.raw` | 200, 1052 bytes |
| the same plus `Authorization: Bearer …` | `Failed to fetch` — preflight rejected |

## What it breaks

`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` is unset in `apps/web/.env`, so the accelerator is the only content source and there is nothing to rotate to. Every block read fails, so:

- the root never adopts, and the resolve tick reports `RefreshVerdict::Unreachable` — the chrome shows `refresh failed: no endpoint served a record this pass could adopt`
- `Drain::load_scope_root` (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:838-852`) cannot assemble the head envelope and returns `Halt::UploadAttempt`, so a queued write never publishes

The write stays `pending` with **no dead letter**, and the status indicator still reads `synced`. A cold start to an empty vault still works, which is why the smoke tier never saw it.

## Reproduction

Against the local stack with `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080`: log in, create a folder, force one refresh pass, wait. The child stays `pending: "metadata"` forever. Allowing `Authorization` in that Kubo's `Gateway.HTTPHeaders` makes the same build pass 11 of 11 web e2e specs.

## Why no test caught it

`crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` builds engines on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` and plants records, so "first-run mint then a queued write drains" is never composed. The gateway tests drive a scripted HTTP fake and assert only that the header is present. CORS exists only in a browser, so the web e2e write path is the first suite in the repo that can catch this class.

## Fix

TLS is the whole rule: a plain-http accelerator falls to `GatewaySource::public` and still serves reads, unauthenticated. That also stops the session token reaching a gateway the host does not own.

## Related, not covered here

Whatever accelerator staging points at must list `Authorization` in its CORS allow-list, or the deployed web app fails the same way.

## The engine defect the new suite caught

The rebase onto main turned all five write specs red, and the cause is #1280,
not the rebase. Since #1243 the engine hands the member's session JWT to any
loopback read accelerator. No browser can deliver it: `Authorization` makes the
cross-origin block read non-simple, and a stock Kubo gateway's CORS allow-list
omits that header, so every preflight is rejected. With `VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS`
unset the accelerator is the only content source, so no block reads at all — the
root never adopts and `Drain::load_scope_root` halts before it publishes. The
write stays pending with **no dead letter** while the chrome still reads
`synced`, which is why the smoke tier never saw it.

`carries_credentials_safely` now admits TLS and nothing else. A leg denied the
token still serves reads unauthenticated, which is what a local Kubo needs, and
the token stops reaching a gateway the host does not own.

This is the class the tier exists for: the engine's gateway tests drive a
scripted HTTP fake, `write_plane.rs` builds on `ApiBaseUrl::offline()` and
plants records, and CORS exists only in a browser.

<result>## Review: `5dfc33553` — accelerator bearer narrowed to `https://`

Verdict: the narrowing is sound and I found **no path where the session token reaches plaintext transport**. Three real gaps, none of them a token-disclosure bug; the most important one is that the fix does not cover the deployed configuration.

### 1. Downgrade paths — clean

- **Redirects are closed at both seams**, so a `https://` → `http://` hop cannot replay the header: `crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs:38` (`redirect::Policy::none()`), `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:29` (`redirect: 'error'`). Covered by `crates/desktop-seams/tests/conformance.rs:476` and `packages/client/src/seams/http.test.ts:125`. The one escape hatch, `ReqwestHttp::with_client` (`crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs:46`), has a single caller and it sets `Policy::none()` (`crates/load/src/seams.rs:24`).
- **Casing / whitespace / scheme-relative all fail closed.** `HTTPS://`, `" https://…"`, `//gw`, `https:/gw` all miss the prefix at `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:178` → the leg is rebuilt via `GatewaySource::public` (`read.rs:218`) and never armed. Both host config edges also trim first: `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts:56-58`, `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/engine/config.rs:89`.
- **Denial is permanent.** `GatewaySource::public` mints a *fresh* cell (`read.rs:146-151`); `SessionBearer::set` is `pub(crate)` and only `ApiClient::with_session_bearer` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1735`) ever writes, into the clone the facade holds (`facade.rs:1651-1665`). A denied leg has no path to being armed by a later login.

### 2. Prefix vs. parse

The prefix is the **right** primitive here, and a URL parse would be strictly *worse*: RFC 3986 schemes are case-insensitive, so a parser would accept `HTTPS://gw.test` and hand it the token, where the prefix denies it. Every parser-vs-prefix divergence I can construct lands on the fail-closed side.

The one input that gets through and probably should not: `REDACTED` passes `read.rs:178` and is handed the bearer. Not a downgrade (still TLS to `gw.cipherbox.test`), and the browser `Request` constructor throws `TypeError` on a credentialed URL so it bricks rather than leaks — but reqwest will send it as Basic auth alongside the JWT. Worth an explicit reject on `@` in the authority, or accept it deliberately and pin it in the test.

### 3. Credential leakage in the read path — clean

`SessionBearer`'s hand-written `Debug` redacts (`read.rs:122-130`); `HttpRequest`'s `Debug` renders header *names* only (`crates/engine/src/seams/http.rs:57-67`); `InvalidBearer` carries nothing (`http.rs:31-33`); the `fetch` refusal string is a static literal (`read.rs:375-377`). Headers are rebuilt per source inside `fetch` (`read.rs:371`), so nothing is retained across a rotation, and `GatewaySource::public` fallbacks hold an unarmable cell. `HttpCredentials::Omit` is pinned on the gateway leg (`read.rs:385`).

### 4. Privacy

An unauthenticated accelerator read exposes **strictly less**: without the JWT the operator sees CIDs + IP + SNI, with it they also get account linkage plus a token that authorizes the whole API. The delta runs the other way — see gap B.

Standing risk this change does not touch: the accelerator is CipherBox's own token-authed Kubo (`CONTEXT.md:81`), and it receives the *full-API* session JWT. A gateway compromise is a session takeover for every online member. TLS is not the mitigation for that; an audience-scoped gateway token is.

---

### Gap A (highest value) — the fix does not cover staging

The commit's stated root cause is CORS, which is **scheme-independent**, but the fix keys on scheme. The read accelerator in staging is a token-authed Kubo behind TLS. If it ships the same stock `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` allow-list, `Authorization` is still attached (`read.rs:212-216`), the preflight is still rejected, and staging bricks in exactly the way the commit message describes — with `Drain::load_scope_root` halting and the chrome still reading `synced`. Confirm the deployed gateway explicitly allows `Authorization` (and that `vars.VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL`, `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml:98`, points at that gateway and not a stock one).

### Gap B — the downgrade is silent, and it can widen the CID audience

`into_gateway` (`read.rs:209-221`) emits no event when it denies the token. If the configured accelerator *requires* auth, every block read now 401s and rotates to `public_fallbacks` — handing the member's read CID set to a third-party gateway that previously never saw it, with no event and no dead letter. That is the same fail-quiet shape the commit message calls out on the write path. Harmless in the shipped local config (`VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` empty) but not in a real deployment. Recommend surfacing the denial once at construction.

### Gap C — the invariant lives at a call site, not in a constructor

`GatewaySource.bearer` is `pub` (`read.rs:141`) and `Gateway.accelerator` is `pub`, so `carries_credentials_safely` guards exactly one call site. Any future in-crate `GatewaySource { base_url, bearer }` bypasses it silently. Make it structural:

```rust
impl GatewaySource {
    /// The only way to attach a credential: TLS or no token.
    pub fn accelerator(base_url: impl Into<String>, bearer: SessionBearer) -> Self {
        let base_url = base_url.into();
        if carries_credentials_safely(&base_url) { Self { base_url, bearer } }
        else { Self::public(base_url) }
    }
}
```

### 5. Tests

Neither updated test is vacuous — `SessionBearer::holding` starts held, so both `is_held()` / `!is_held()` assertions have real polarity. But both are **config-level only**: the doc comment's claim that "a leg denied the token still serves reads, unauthenticated" is never asserted on the wire. The only wire-level no-`AUTHORIZATION` assertion is on the *public fallback* leg (`read.rs:643-648`), not on a denied accelerator.

Worth adding, in `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs`:

```rust
// The prefix-vs-parse divergence, frozen: a parser would accept these.
#[test]
fn an_uppercase_or_padded_https_scheme_is_denied_the_bearer() {
    for base_url in ["HTTPS://gw.cipherbox.test", "Https://gw.cipherbox.test",
                     " https://gw.cipherbox.test", "https:/gw.cipherbox.test",
                     "https:gw.cipherbox.test"] { /* !is_held() */ }
}

// Decide and pin: today this IS handed the bearer.
#[test]
fn an_https_url_with_embedded_credentials_is_denied_the_bearer() {}

// The doc comment's second half, asserted on the wire rather than the config.
#[test]
fn a_plain_http_accelerator_is_still_consulted_and_carries_no_authorization() {
    // GatewayConfig { accelerator: Some("http://127.0.0.1:8080"), .. }
    // -> read_block -> requests()[0].url starts with the accelerator
    // -> and no AUTHORIZATION header
}

// Denial survives a later login (facade-level).
#[test]
fn a_login_after_construction_cannot_arm_a_plain_http_accelerator() {}
```

The last one is the one that would catch a regression in Gap C.</result>

The fix lands in #1246 (`carries_credentials_safely` admits TLS and nothing else, and `GatewaySource::accelerator` is now the only way a leg receives the bearer). Three things the security and crypto reviews of that diff surfaced are **not** fixed there and want their own decision:

**1. The failure is undiagnosable, which is why this cost a day.** Every non-2xx — 401 and 403 included — hits the bare `continue` in `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:320-322`, and the exhausted source set surfaces as `ReadError::Unavailable`. `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:853` then maps any head-assembly error to `Halt::UploadAttempt`: a charged retry with no operator-visible reason. The member sees a write that stays pending, no dead letter, and a status indicator reading `synced`. The trust verdict is right — a 401 is not an integrity signal — but nothing distinguishes "the gateway refuses me" from "the block is not there yet".

**2. Denying the token is silent, and it can widen the CID audience.** `into_gateway` emits no event when it withholds the bearer. If a deployment's accelerator *requires* auth, every read now 401s and rotates to `public_fallbacks` — handing the member's read CID set to a third-party gateway that never saw it before, with no event. The shipped local config leaves `VITE_PUBLIC_GATEWAYS` empty, so nothing rotates today; a real deployment is a different matter. Surfacing the denial once at construction would cover both this and item 1.

**3. A second, weaker credential policy exists.** The load harness sends `LOAD_TEST_GATEWAY_TOKEN` to any scheme, `http://localhost:8080` included — `crates/load/src/runner.rs:87-98`, default at `crates/load/src/plan.rs:122`. It never consults `carries_credentials_safely`. Pre-existing and outside the fix.

Also worth pinning before anyone points the accelerator at a deployed gateway: the CORS half of this is scheme-independent. A stock Kubo over TLS rejects the `Authorization` preflight exactly as the loopback one did, so the deployed gateway must list that header explicitly. Today no accelerator is configured anywhere — `vars.VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` exists at neither repo nor `staging` scope, and the staging Kubo gateway is bound loopback-only with no vhost — so nothing is broken in a deployment right now.

Both review gates are back and folded in. Summary while CI settles.

**Crypto/privacy review** — no token-disclosure path found. Redirects are closed at both HTTP seams (`crates/desktop-seams/src/http.rs:38`, `packages/client/src/seams/http.ts:29`), `SessionBearer`'s `Debug` redacts, and a denied leg gets a fresh cell nothing can arm later. Three gaps, two of which I fixed:

- The invariant guarded one call site while both `GatewaySource` fields are public. `GatewaySource::accelerator` is now the only way a source receives the bearer.
- `REDACTED` passed the check and reqwest would send Basic auth beside the JWT. Denied now, and pinned by a test.

**Security review** — fail-closed behaviour holds: verification runs after the fetch and is independent of the bearer, so a tampered block is still a terminal `TrustViolation` (`crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:333-335`). No deployment loses acceleration: every configured accelerator in the repo is a local Kubo needing no auth, and `vars.VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` exists at neither repo nor `staging` scope. No read passes through the API, so no quota changes. It found two comment defects, both fixed:

- The retained "stale or mistyped" clause was false under the new rule — a mistyped `https` host still receives the token. The rule is transport confidentiality, and the comment now says only that.
- The CORS paragraph justified "do not send `Authorization` to a stock Kubo", not "TLS only" — a stock gateway over TLS rejects the same preflight. It no longer sits in the code as if the scheme solved it. The reason lives in the commit message and issue #1280, where it is accurate.

A test name also claimed more than the rule does, since loopback URLs physically *can* keep a credential. It is now `an_accelerator_that_is_not_plain_tls_is_never_handed_a_credential`.

Three findings I did **not** fix, recorded as a comment on #1280:

1. The failure is undiagnosable, which is what made this cost a day: every non-2xx becomes `ReadError::Unavailable`, and `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:853` maps any head-assembly error to `Halt::UploadAttempt` — a charged retry with no reason, no dead letter, and a `synced` indicator.
2. Withholding the token emits no event, so an accelerator that *requires* auth would rotate the member's CID set to third-party gateways silently.
3. The load harness sends its gateway token to any scheme (`crates/load/src/runner.rs:87-98`) — a second, weaker policy that never consults this rule.

`1e898b4eb` is pushed. Locally after the changes: engine suite 978 unit tests plus every integration target green, clippy clean, and the web e2e suite 13 passed against a stock-CORS Kubo. On CI, 13 checks green and 14 still running with no failure, `Web E2E Smoke` among them. I will report when it settles.

Issue #1280 holds the regression, and a comment on it holds the three findings I left unfixed: the undiagnosable read failure, the silent token denial, and the load harness's second credential policy.

## The UAT stack is up

The #1247 download check is unchanged from my earlier message: sign in at http://localhost:4173, confirm `navigator.serviceWorker.controller !== null` before you click, upload a file, then read the `/stream/<uuid>` response in the Network tab. A 394-byte `text/html` body is the bug; the pipe's `cache-control: no-store` and `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` headers are the correct path.

Two local-stack changes I made along the way, both outside the PR: `THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT=200` in `apps/api/.env`, and the mock routing store now runs from source on the host because its container image was stale and its Dockerfile fails to rebuild.

input.content:
Rejected, for three reasons.

Correctness does not rest on the cache key. Cargo's own fingerprint carries the rustc version, so a `target/` restored under a changed toolchain is rebuilt rather than reused. The cost of a toolchain-only change is a wasted restore, never a stale artifact.

The change is outside this PR. All ten exact keys in `ci.yml` predate it — this diff adds `restore-keys` fallbacks and touches no `key:` line. Rewriting every one of them, `macos-cargo-`, `windows-cargo-` and the desktop matrix included, reaches three jobs the PR deliberately leaves alone.

It would also evict the whole set at once. Every exact key changes value on the same commit, so every PR-scoped entry is cold on the next run, in a repo whose cache budget is already over the limit — which is the reason this PR seeds two entries rather than one per job prefix.

The seed keys hash both files on purpose: they are written once per main-push and must not outlive a toolchain change. Consumers reach them by the `main-cargo-` / `main-wasm-cargo-` prefix, so the two key shapes do not have to match.

content.text:
Done. CodeRabbit reviewed the head at `1e898b4eb` — 3 actionable comments and 1 nitpick — and all are answered. CI on the new head: **35 of 35 green**.

## Threads

| Thread | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/engine/src/content/read.rs:197` — reject ambiguous authorities | **Fixed** in `94a9bd0a5` |
| `tests/web-e2e/README.md:65` — the API holds the terminal | **Fixed** in `94a9bd0a5` |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml:225` — hash `rust-toolchain.toml` in every cache key | **Rejected**, with reasons |

The engine one was a real hole in the gate I added an hour ago. `carries_credentials_safely` refused `REDACTED` but not the same URL a slash short: `https:///member:secret@gw.cipherbox.test` splits to an **empty** authority, which holds no `@`, so it passed and the bearer was attached. A URL parser reads that userinfo as the path, so the host the token would reach is not the configured one. The gate now requires a non-empty authority, and both extra-slash forms plus bare `https://` joined the rejection test.

The README fix is the papercut I hit myself this session: step 2 ran `node apps/api/dist/main.js` in the foreground, so steps 3 and 4 had nowhere to run. It now starts in the background behind the same `curl --retry --retry-connrefused` readiness check the workflow uses.

I rejected the cache-key one on three grounds: cargo's own fingerprint carries the rustc version, so a restore under a changed toolchain is rebuilt rather than reused — the cost is a wasted restore, never a stale artifact; all ten exact keys predate this PR, which adds `restore-keys` and touches no `key:` line, so the change reaches three jobs the PR deliberately leaves alone; and every key would change value on one commit, evicting the whole set in a repo already over its cache budget.

## Nitpick

One nitpick, five comments in `files.page.ts`, no thread — dispositioned per item in a PR comment. Two taken: the doc comments on `open` and `preview` restated their own names and are gone. Three kept: `move`'s records that the destination must be a child of the open folder, which the signature does not carry; `upload`'s records that the suite drives the file input rather than simulating a drop; and `act`'s is what makes an opaquely named private helper readable at five call sites.

Local gates before the push: engine read tests 25 passed, clippy clean, typecheck, lint and tracker-refs clean, and the web e2e suite 13 passed against the stock-CORS Kubo.

Head is now `94a9bd0a5`, with zero unresolved threads. The UAT stack is still up and unchanged — API :3000, routing :3001, e2e bundle :4173, shipping bundle :4174.

content.text:
Your result and my probes disagree, so the difference is worth pinning down before anyone writes a fix.

Against the same bundle on :4173, the worker **does** serve that prefix here — I checked two ways just now:

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch('/stream/not-a-real-ticket')` | `404`, empty body — the pipe's own answer |
| iframe navigation to `/stream/not-a-real-ticket` | empty document — the pipe again |
| iframe navigation to `/no-such-route` | 377-byte app shell — the SPA fallback, as expected |

So both a script fetch and a navigation reach `MediaPipe.respond` (`packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:89-91`, routed at `packages/client/src/sw/install.ts:109-113`). Your 394 bytes is `dist/index.html` served by vite preview, which means your request reached the origin instead. Three things produce that, and they need different fixes:

1. **DevTools bypass.** Application → Service Workers has a *Bypass for network* checkbox. Checked, every request skips the worker while `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` stays non-null — so `MediaService.streaming` is still true, the stream path still runs, and the origin answers with the shell. That reproduces your exact symptom and is not an app defect.
2. **The tab was not controlled at click time**, and something else kept `streaming` true.
3. **The anchor-download request genuinely escapes the worker in your Chrome** while a plain fetch does not. That would be a real platform-level finding, and the fix is to stop relying on `<a download>` for the stream path rather than to patch the worker.

Run this in the console of the tab you tested, before anything else:

```js
(await fetch('/stream/probe')).status
```

- `404` → the worker is serving the prefix in your session, so the download click specifically escaped it. That is case 3, and I will take it from there.
- `200` → the worker is bypassed in that tab. Uncheck *Bypass for network*, reload once, confirm `navigator.serviceWorker.controller !== null`, and repeat the save. If the file is then correct, #1247 is a test-condition artefact and the PR's workaround can go; if it is still 394 bytes, we are back to case 3 with the bypass ruled out.

Also worth telling me: which port you used, and whether the Network tab entry for `/stream/<uuid>` showed a *Service Worker* source or a plain network one.

content.text:
Proven, and it is the app's design, not your test conditions. I served the same bundle from a logging origin on :4175 and issued three requests from one tab under one controlling worker:

| request | reached the origin? |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch('/stream/fetch-probe')` | no — the worker answered, 404 |
| iframe navigation to `/stream/iframe-probe` | no — the worker answered |
| `<a download href="/stream/anchor-probe">` click | **yes — `HIT GET /stream/anchor-probe`** |

Chromium does not dispatch a request initiated by an anchor's `download` attribute to the service worker. `useFileDownload` mints a correct ticket, the worker is ready to serve it, and the click walks straight past it to the origin — which answers every unknown path with `index.html`. That is your 394 bytes, and no amount of worker-side work can catch it, because the worker is never asked.

**The fix**: trigger the save by navigating rather than by clicking a download anchor, since navigations do reach the pipe.

1. `packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts` — set `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=UTF-8''…` on the ticket response, which is what turns a navigation into a save. The filename comes from the vault and the port is untrusted input, so it needs the same clamping treatment `safeMimeType` already gets.
2. The ticket registration carries a mime type today (`streamTicket(media, node, size, OPAQUE)`); it gains the filename alongside it.
3. `apps/web/src/hooks/useFileDownload.ts` — `saveToDisk` navigates a hidden iframe to the ticket URL for the stream path. The buffered blob path keeps the anchor, which works because a `blob:` URL never involves the worker.

That also removes the failure mode where a wrong file lands on disk at all: nothing is written unless the pipe serves it.

Two things worth knowing before I start. Main already detects this case — `save` returns `refused` with a `NEVER_FETCHED` error when the pipe saw no read — so tell me whether the UI showed you an error alongside the bad file, because that tells us whether the detection fires and only the file is wrong. And the round-trip spec in the suite asserts through the preview precisely to avoid this path; once the save is trusted, that workaround comes out, which is what #1247 says.

Say go and I will branch off main and implement it, with a web-e2e case that fails on today's code.

fix(web): drive a ticket save as a navigation so the worker serves it

Chromium issues an `<a download>` request without dispatching it to the
Service Worker. The save minted a correct ticket and clicked a link at it, so
the request walked past the pipe to the origin, which answers every unknown
path with the SPA fallback: the member received a 394-byte `index.html` under
their file's name.

Measured from one tab under one controlling worker, against a logging origin:
a `fetch` of a ticket path never reached it, an iframe navigation to the same
path never reached it, and the link click did.

So the save navigates a hidden frame instead, and the pipe's head carries
`content-disposition` to make that navigation a file rather than a document.
The name is percent-encoded to RFC 8187 `attr-char`, which is what keeps a
vault-chosen name from forging a header or a second parameter, and the worker
re-checks that exact shape before it serves one — the port is untrusted input
there, as it already is for the content type. A blob save keeps the link: a
`blob:` URL never involves the worker.

`save-path.spec.ts` asserts the saved bytes through the shipped chrome. On the
link form it fails with 353 bytes of `<!doctype html`, which is the defect.

<result>## Verdict

The header-injection surface is genuinely closed, and the render path is untouched. I found **one real defect** (availability, multi-tab), plus a few notes. Nothing that leaks plaintext or lets a vault-chosen name escape the header.

---

### 1. Header injection — clean, both layers agree

`packages/client/src/media/range.ts:61` — `ATTR_CHAR = /[A-Za-z0-9!#$&+\-.^_\`|~]/` is **exactly** RFC 8187 `attr-char` (ALPHA / DIGIT / `!#$&+-.^_\`|~`). `^` is not in leading position so it is literal; `\-` is literal. Everything else — `"` `;` `,` space CR LF `*` `'` `=` and every byte ≥ 0x80 — is percent-encoded (`range.ts:63-68`, encoding UTF-8 bytes, so multi-byte names are handled correctly). No second parameter, no second header, no change of disposition type is reachable from a name.

`packages/client/src/sw/pipe.ts:392` — `SAFE_DISPOSITION` is anchored `^…$` (JS `$` does *not* match before a trailing `\n`, unlike Python/Ruby), and has a single `*` over a flat character class inside one optional group — linear, no catastrophic backtracking. Two ports appending two `content-disposition` headers is also handled: `Headers.get` joins with `", "`, which fails the regex and clamps to bare `attachment`.

The only divergence between the two: the worker's class adds `%` unconditionally (`pipe.ts:392`), so it accepts `%`/`%ZZ` sequences the encoder would never mint. Harmless — `%` is not a delimiter, and a decoded `%3B` lands inside the filename value after parameter parsing, not in the header grammar.

Residual (unchanged by this PR): the decoded filename can still contain `/`, `..`, NUL, or an RTL override — defense is the browser's download-filename sanitizer, exactly as it was for the old `<a download>` attribute. Not a regression.

### 2. Render path — not weakened

`apps/web/src/hooks/useFilePreview.ts:62` calls `streamTicket` with four args, so `downloadName` is `undefined` and `range.ts:83` pushes no header. The player never gets a disposition. `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox` and the `safeMimeType` clamp in `pipe.ts:378-381` are applied identically on both paths; the disposition is additive.

One thing this design now depends on that it did not before: **CSP `sandbox` on the response is what keeps the frame unreadable.** If the pipe ever serves a ticket body without a disposition, the response commits as a document *inside a same-origin frame the app owns*; `sandbox` gives it an opaque origin so `frame.contentDocument` is null. Dropping that header from `sealed()` would turn the hidden frame into readable plaintext. Worth a comment at `pipe.ts:381` — it is currently justified only as anti-execution.

### 3. The iframe — no new exposure

The ticket URL was already in the DOM as `link.href`, and any same-origin script can `fetch()` it regardless. The frame adds nothing an XSS did not already have. A cross-origin embedder cannot read either. `whenIdle` (`packages/client/src/media/broker.ts:153-176`) resolves only when no cursor holds the ticket, and a reader *between windows* still counts, so a stalled or paused download cannot be revoked out from under itself. `revoke` (`broker.ts:200`) therefore only ever fires after the worker's body already closed — the remaining bytes are the browser's. The security review found a real defect in my first cut, and confirming it changed the fix.

**The multi-tab defect.** A navigation carries no client id, so the worker borrows whichever tab brokered last. I reproduced it in Chrome: with a second tab open, the save sat for 30 s and then reported *"the browser did not start the download"* — the borrowed port belonged to the other tab, whose registry never minted that ticket. `saveAll` stops at a refusal, so one stale tab would kill a whole batch. `9c0b09660` makes an anonymous request that the borrowed port refuses ask the other ports; a request that names its client keeps its own port, so the per-client isolation the suite asserts is untouched. A ticket is a random capability only its minting registry can redeem, so asking a tab that does not hold it discloses nothing.

**The rest of the review.** No header-injection path: the encoder is exactly RFC 8187 `attr-char`, the worker's re-check is anchored with no backtracking, and two ports appending two dispositions joins to a value that fails the check and clamps to bare `attachment`. The render path is untouched — the preview passes no name, so the player gets no disposition. The hidden frame adds nothing an XSS did not already have, and it is removed on every path. No truncation: the revoke waits on a reader that counts as busy between windows.

Three things it flagged that I acted on:

- The CSP `sandbox` is now load-bearing beyond execution — it is what keeps plaintext unreadable if a body ever commits as a document in that frame. Said so at the header, where the rationale lives.
- The spec used an all-`attr-char` name and a 60-byte payload, so neither the percent-encoding nor the revoke race was exercised. It now saves `notes — édition 1.md` and a payload past one window.
- A doc comment was stranded above the new page-object method. Moved back onto `act`.

**Both guards are proven by removal.** With the save put back on a link, the byte assertion fails with `<!doctype html`. With the fan-out taken out, the two-tab spec fails and the single-tab one passes.

/** Opens the ticket on one port; `null` when the port went dead and was discarded. */
private async tryPort(port: MessagePortLike, ticket: string, range: string | null): Promise<Response | null> {
  const requestId = this.nextRequestId;
  this.nextRequestId += 1;
  const head = await this.open(port, requestId, ticket, range);
  if (!head) {
    this.post(port, { type: 'cb:media:close', requestId });
    this.discardPort(port);
    return null;
  }
  if (head.status !== 200 && head.status !== 206) {
    this.post(port, { type: 'cb:media:close', requestId });
    return sealed(head.status, head.headers);
  }
  return sealed(head.status, head.headers, this.body(port, requestId));
}

`range.ts:61` `ATTR_CHAR = /[A-Za-z0-9!#$&+\-.^_\`|~]/` and `pipe.ts:435` `SAFE_DISPOSITION = /^attachment(; filename\*=UTF-8''[A-Za-z0-9!#$&+\-.^_\`|~%]*)?$/` are the same set, maintained independently, and each carries a comment pointing at the other (`range.ts:58-59`, `pipe.ts:429-433`). Drift makes the worker clamp names the encoder legitimately mints. `pipe.ts` already imports `safeMimeType` from `../media/range.js`, so export the charset instead:

```ts
// range.ts
/** RFC 8187 `attr-char` — the only bytes a name keeps into the header. */
export const ATTR_CHARS = "A-Za-z0-9!#$&+\\-.^_`|~";
const ATTR_CHAR = new RegExp(`[${ATTR_CHARS}]`);

// pipe.ts
const SAFE_DISPOSITION = new RegExp(`^attachment(; filename\\*=UTF-8''[${ATTR_CHARS}%]*)?$`);
```

Both cross-referencing comments then reduce to one line each. If you prefer two literal regexes for greppability, at minimum delete one of the two paragraphs — the pipe-side one is the one that needs a why (untrusted port), the range-side one only needs "RFC 8187 `attr-char`; everything else is percent-encoded".

On the encoder itself: the manual `TextEncoder` + allowlist at `range.ts:63-68` is longer than `encodeURIComponent(name).replace(/['()*!~]/g, …)`, but it is fail-closed by construction and matches the clamp exactly. Keep it — noting it here so it does not get re-litigated in review.

## 4. Small shape fixes

- `range.ts:71` — `export function contentDisposition` has no consumer outside the file (no test imports it, not in `packages/client/src/index.ts`). Drop the `export`.
- `useFileDownload.ts:157-163` — returning a teardown closure buys nothing over returning the frame, and it forces the "returns the teardown" sentence in the doc and the meaningless name `done`. Make it `function ticketFrame(url: string): HTMLIFrameElement` returning `frame`, use `const frame = ticketFrame(ticket)` at :82 and `frame.remove()` at :97. The comment at :95-96 then fits on one line: `// The browser owns the transfer once the read settles, so this cannot cut it.`
- `pipe.ts:414-418` — the appended "The sandbox is load-bearing beyond execution…" defends the pre-existing CSP line that this diff does not touch; that is the unchanged-code apologia shape in `AGENTS.md`. Either drop it or reduce to one clause on the frame side, where the frame is created.
- `packages/client/src/media/range.ts:12-22` `MediaPresentation` — verdict: keep. `MediaSource extends MediaPresentation` keeps the dependency pointing `registry → range` (the reverse would be circular), and it saves threading two scalars through `baseHeaders`/`whole`/`partial`. It is the simplest thing that works.
- `apps/web/src/lib/streamTicket.ts:12` optional `downloadName` — verdict: keep, it has both a with- and a without- caller (`useFileDownload.ts:79`, `useFilePreview.ts:62`). One optional improvement: `mimeType` and `downloadName` are two adjacent strings that a caller can silently transpose; folding them into a single `presentation: MediaPresentation` param (exported from `@cipherbox/client`) makes that impossible and reuses the new type. Worth it only if you are happy adding the index export.

## 5. Tests

`packages/client/src/media/range.test.ts:143-177` — all five cases carry distinct weight (absent header, both statuses, header-forging chars, multi-byte UTF-8, empty-encode fallback); no restatements. Good as-is.

`packages/client/src/sw/pipe.test.ts`:
- The three new routing tests are each a distinct claim (fan-out finds the minter; all-404 answers 404; a named client is never fanned out). Keep all three.
- The 404-answering `FakePort` is constructed inline four times (`:554-562`, `:578-586` as the local `deny`, `:603-611`). The file already has `streamingPort` (:32) and `stalledPort` (:53) factories — add `unknownTicketPort()` beside them and use it in all three tests.
- `:881` `it(\`${name}\`, …)` → `it(name, …)`.
- The disposition table (`:869-902`) is well-chosen; "serves the shape the tab mints" and "serves a bare attachment" are the two legal shapes, not a restatement of each other.

`apps/web` unit tests:
- The `HTMLElement.prototype.append` patch is duplicated verbatim — `useFileDownload.test.ts:104-113` and `FileBrowserActions.test.tsx:828-833` — including the awkward `as typeof HTMLElement.prototype.append` cast, and the two files record different shapes (`requested: string[]` merged with clicks vs. separate `clicked`/`navigated`). `apps/web/src/test/` is the existing home for shared fakes (`storeFakes.ts`, `authFakes.tsx`). Extract `apps/web/src/test/saveSpy.ts` exporting something like `trackSaves(): { clicked: {href,download}[]; navigated: (string|null)[]; restore(): void }` and use it in both. That deletes the six-line `requested` doc block at `useFileDownload.test.ts:92-96` outright, and removes the loss of resolution that merging clicks and frames into one array introduced (a regression that navigated a frame to a `blob:` URL currently still passes `expect(requested).toEqual(['blob:fake/1', …])`).
- `useFileDownload.test.ts:335` — the test is named "navigates a frame **rather than clicking a download link**", but nothing in it asserts that no link was clicked; it only inspects `frames`. Either add `expect(clicked).toEqual([])` (free once finding 5 lands) or rename it to the claim it actually proves — the teardown timing, e.g. `'keeps the frame alive until the read settles, then drops it'`. The "not a link" claim is already proven at `FileBrowserActions.test.tsx:860`, so renaming is the tighter option and removes the overlap between the two files.

input.content:
Closes #1247

A save wrote the app shell to disk. `useFileDownload` minted a correct ticket
and clicked `<a download href="/stream/<ticket>">` at it — and **Chromium
issues an `<a download>` request without dispatching it to the Service
Worker**, so the request walked past the pipe to the origin, which answers
every unknown path with `index.html`. The member received 394 bytes under their
file's name.

Measured from one tab, under one controlling worker, against a logging origin:

| request | reached the origin? |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch('/stream/…')` | no — the worker answered |
| iframe navigation to `/stream/…` | no — the worker answered |
| `<a download href="/stream/…">` click | **yes** |

Nothing worker-side could have caught it, because the worker is never asked.

## The save is a navigation now

A hidden frame is navigated to the ticket, and the pipe's head carries
`content-disposition`, which is what makes that navigation a file rather than a
document. The name is percent-encoded to RFC 8187 `attr-char`, so a
vault-chosen name carries no quote, no semicolon and no newline into the
header, and the worker re-checks that exact shape before serving it — the port
is untrusted input there, as it already was for the content type. Anything else
is served as a bare `attachment`, which still saves.

A blob save keeps the link: a `blob:` URL never involves the worker.

## A save reaches the tab that minted it

A navigation carries no client id, so the pipe borrows whichever tab brokered
last. With a second tab open that is the wrong registry, which answers 404, and
the save fails 30 s later as "the browser did not start the download" — taking
a whole `saveAll` batch with it, because a refusal stops the loop. Reproduced
in Chrome with two tabs.

An anonymous request refused by the borrowed port now asks the others, and only
the tab that minted the ticket can answer. A request that names its client
keeps its own port, whatever any other tab holds: the fan-out is for
navigations alone. A ticket is a random same-origin capability that only its
minting registry redeems, so asking a tab that does not hold it discloses
nothing it could not already read off the DOM.

## Verification

Both fixes are guarded, and both guards were proven by removal — the point of a
regression test is that it fails on the code without the fix:

- `save-path.spec.ts` asserts the saved bytes through the shipped chrome. Put
  the save back on a link and it fails with 353 bytes whose head decodes as
  `<!doctype html`.
- Its second case opens a second tab before saving. Take the fan-out out and it
  fails while the single-tab case passes.

The spec also pins the decoded filename and that the transfer came from
`/stream/`, so it cannot pass by quietly taking the buffered path. It saves
`notes — édition 1.md` to exercise the percent-encoded header end to end, and a
payload past one `MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES` so the revoke that follows the transfer
has a race to lose.

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs` — clean.
- `pnpm test` — 1080 across the five packages.
- `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web-e2e test:e2e` against a live local stack — 15
  passed.

## Reviews folded in

A security pass found the multi-tab defect above, and that the pipe's `sandbox`
is load-bearing beyond execution — it is what keeps plaintext out of the
frame's reach if a body ever commits as a document there. That note now sits at
the frame it protects.

A quality pass collapsed what the first cut duplicated: the `<a download>`
rationale stated six times, the open-close-seal sequence written twice, the
`attr-char` set written twice where drift would clamp names the encoder mints,
and a save spy copied across two test files — which also cost resolution, since
a frame navigated to a `blob:` URL satisfied the buffered-path assertions.

## Not fixed here

The round trip in `write-path.spec.ts` still asserts through the preview rather
than the save. It can move onto the save affordance now that one is trusted;
that is a change to a spec this PR does not otherwise touch.

PR #1282 is open as a draft: **https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1282** — *fix: save a file through the Service Worker instead of past it*, three commits, `Closes #1247`.

## What it fixes

**The save wrote the app shell.** `useFileDownload` minted a correct ticket and clicked a download link at it, and Chromium issues an `<a download>` request without dispatching it to the worker — so it walked past the pipe to the origin, which answers unknown paths with `index.html`. Your 394 bytes. The save is now a frame navigation, and the pipe's `content-disposition` is what makes that navigation a file. The name is percent-encoded to RFC 8187 `attr-char`, and the worker re-checks that exact shape before serving it.

**A second tab broke every save.** Found by the security pass, confirmed in Chrome: a navigation carries no client id, so the pipe borrowed whichever tab brokered last, whose registry never minted the ticket — 30 s, then "the browser did not start the download", and a whole `saveAll` batch with it. An anonymous request refused by the borrowed port now asks the others; a request that names its client keeps its own port.

## Both guards proven by removal

- Put the save back on a link → the byte assertion fails with `<!doctype html`.
- Take the fan-out out → the two-tab case fails while the single-tab one passes.

The spec also pins the decoded filename and that the transfer came from `/stream/`, so it cannot pass by quietly taking the buffered path. It saves `notes — édition 1.md` and a payload past one window, so the encoding and the revoke race are both exercised.

## Review gates

Security found the multi-tab defect and that the pipe's `sandbox` is load-bearing beyond execution — that note now sits at the frame it protects. The quality pass collapsed what my first cut duplicated: the same rationale in six places, the open-close-seal sequence written twice, the `attr-char` set written twice where drift would clamp valid names, and a save spy copied across two test files — which also cost resolution, since a frame navigated to a `blob:` URL satisfied the buffered-path assertions.

Local gates: typecheck, lint, tracker refs clean; 1080 unit tests; web e2e 15 passed. CI is running and I will report when it settles.

One thing I deliberately left: `write-path.spec.ts` still reads back through the preview. That workaround exists because the save was not trusted, and it can move onto the save affordance now — but that is a change to a spec this PR does not otherwise touch.

content.text:
Crypto-privacy pass is clean. What I checked, and what it found:

- **Header injection through `content-disposition`.** The clamp is anchored at both ends, and JS `$` does not match before a trailing newline (verified, not assumed — `attachment\nx-evil: 1` and `…''a\n` both clamp). A duplicate append reads back as `attachment, attachment`, which also clamps. `Headers.append` rejects a newline value on top of that.
- **Ticket confidentiality under fan-out.** A ticket is `crypto.randomUUID()`, and the fan-out offers it only to ports the worker holds — all same-origin windows, which have no boundary against the minting tab to begin with. A tab that did not mint it learns a string it cannot redeem.
- **Fail-closed direction.** The fan-out is reached only when the request names no client. A request that names one keeps its own port whatever any other tab holds, so the identified case cannot be widened by this change.
- **No CORS header is ever set**, so a cross-origin load stays opaque; and a 404 from a borrowed port closes its cursor before the next port is asked, so a fan-out pins no stream.

Recording that on the PR and flipping it to ready.
